parts.note: ante is Latin for before, as in ante-room
post is Latin for after, as in postscript

explanation.surface: A gambler bets both before and after something happens.
explanation.walkthrough: Ante-post betting is a British racing term: bets placed on a race well before the day, often before the runners are declared.
explanation.definitionFit: Ante-post describes wagers struck in advance of race day, so it is a kind of betting.

explanation.surface: Someone fakes being moved by another's emotions.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both to feign and to move emotionally, two separate senses.

indicators.note: the synonym for go goes round the I

parts.note: your go is your turn

explanation.surface: I go round a city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go round' looks like one phrase for TURN, but only 'go' gives TURN; 'round' puts it around I.
explanation.definitionFit: Turin is a city in north-west Italy.

indicators.note: the engagement is placed in the Frenchman's name

parts.note: Pierre is a typical French man's name
a date is an appointment or engagement

explanation.surface: A Frenchman has an engagement in his second home.
explanation.walkthrough: Pierre stands for any Frenchman, a common crossword convention; the definition is the French phrase's English sense of a second home.
explanation.definitionFit: A pied-a-terre is a small second home kept for occasional stays.

indicators.note: only part of the word co-starring is used, a run inside it

explanation.surface: Jack is co-starring in a part.
explanation.definitionFit: Jack and tar are both old slang words for a sailor.

clue.text: Man on whom success depends gets an honour, gold

parts.note: CH, Companion of Honour, is a British order
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: The key man in a team is rewarded with an honour and a gold medal.
explanation.definitionFit: The anchor of a team or show is the mainstay whose performance holds it together.

parts.note: reads like a car in neutral, but gear here means clothes

explanation.surface: A car is out of gear.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with no clothes on is naked, out of their gear.

clue.text: Lone whale swimming at the end of last month

indicators.note: the letters of lone whale move about freely

explanation.surface: A solitary whale swam about at the end of October.
explanation.walkthrough: The puzzle appeared in November, so last month's end was 31 October.
explanation.definitionFit: Halloween falls on 31 October, the close of the month before this puzzle's publication.

clue.text: Animal that's strange at home with hill-dweller

parts.note: rum is British slang for odd or strange
in means at home
ants live in anthills

explanation.surface: An odd animal lives at home with someone from the hills.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruminant, such as a cow, is a cud-chewing animal.

clue.text: Plant hairs as you might say

indicators.note: signals that a word is to be spoken and its sound taken

parts.note: furs are animal coats of hair

explanation.surface: A plant has hairs, so to speak.
explanation.definitionFit: Furze is another name for gorse, a spiny yellow-flowered shrub.

clue.text: Big hit when one doesn't miss a trick

definitions.meaning: in baseball, a home run with the bases loaded is the biggest possible hit

definitions.text: when one doesn't miss a trick
definitions.meaning: in bridge, winning all thirteen tricks of a deal earns the top bonus

explanation.surface: A hard blow is struck by someone who stays alert.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names both a bases-loaded home run and a bridge contract taking every trick.

clue.text: Benevolent, suitable character, head of department

parts.note: good means fit or suitable
one's nature is one's character

indicators.note: takes the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A kindly department head with a suitable character.
explanation.definitionFit: Good-natured means kindly and well disposed, much as benevolent does.

definitions.meaning: to come close to something, as a figure nears a total

explanation.surface: An approach that is more or less right.
explanation.definitionFit: As verb it means come close to; as adjective it means nearly exact.

clue.text: Is able to record Louise getting stuck into melon

parts.note: is able means can

indicators.note: one piece is lodged inside another, as if pushed in

parts.note: to tape is to record
Lou is a short form of Louise

explanation.surface: Someone can make a recording of Louise tucking into a melon.
explanation.definitionFit: The cantaloupe is a variety of melon with orange flesh.

clue.text: Jonathan, about one, to meet and become member

indicators.note: Jonathan's short form goes about, or around, the other piece

parts.note: Jon is a short form of Jonathan
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Jonathan, roughly one o'clock, arrives to sign up as a member.
explanation.definitionFit: To join is both to link up with and to enrol in a club, covering both senses given.

clue.text: Class total disrupted regardless of the consequences

indicators.note: the letters of class total are thrown out of order

explanation.surface: A class's total was disrupted, whatever the consequences.
explanation.definitionFit: At all costs is an idiom meaning whatever happens, regardless of the price.

parts.note: recalls the children's song about ten such bottles hanging on the wall, one falling at a time

explanation.surface: A fly is one of ten things hanging up.
explanation.walkthrough: The British counting song 'Ten Green Bottles' has the bottles 'hanging on the wall'; the answer is also a metallic green blowfly.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a common blowfly with a shiny metallic green body.

clue.text: Present stallion shouldn't be taken to dentist

parts.note: a present is a gift
a stallion is a male horse

explanation.surface: Advice that a stallion given as a present should not visit the dentist.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on the proverb 'never look a gift horse in the mouth': do not inspect the teeth of an animal given free.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb says such an animal's mouth must not be examined, the job a dentist does.

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A character makes an appearance in the opening chapter of a novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Chi is a Greek letter, and a letter of an alphabet is a character.

clue.text: Neat gash free from infection at the start

indicators.note: the piece for free from infection comes at the start

parts.note: a clean wound is free from infection
a cut is a gash

explanation.surface: A neat gash that was free from infection at the start.
explanation.definitionFit: Clean-cut means neat and sharply defined, or tidy in appearance.

indicators.note: the first letter of the synonym is cut off

parts.note: something left is remaining

explanation.surface: An amphibian survives with its head gone.
explanation.definitionFit: An eft is a newt, especially a young one, a small amphibian.

parts.note: playing second fiddle means being subordinate; read literally, the orchestra's leading violinist is the one who plays the top part

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to take a subordinate role.
explanation.definitionFit: The leader of an orchestra's first section plays the principal violin part rather than the second.

indicators.note: the synonym for scurry is read backwards

parts.note: to dart is to scurry
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen's royal cipher

explanation.surface: Someone scurries back to the Queen's merchant.
explanation.definitionFit: A trader buys and sells goods, as a merchant does.

clue.text: Say about husband going in pale

indicators.note: the husband piece goes into the rearranged letters
about signals the letters of say are moved around

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that a husband entering looks pale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges SAY into ASY, and 'going in' puts H inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashy means ash-coloured, a greyish pallor.

clue.text: Barker travelling round bay to emerge into the open

indicators.note: the reworked letters go round the bay piece
the letters of barker are on the move into a new order

parts.note: a cove is a small bay

explanation.surface: A barking dog roams around the bay before coming out into view.
explanation.walkthrough: 'travelling' rearranges the letters of Barker into BREAKR, which goes round the bay piece; the surface's dog is a red herring.
explanation.definitionFit: To break cover is the hunting idiom for an animal leaving its hiding place.

definitions.meaning: a bound is a leap or jump
an underground storeroom, as for wine

explanation.surface: Something is heading for the cellar.
explanation.definitionFit: A vault is both a leap over something and an underground chamber.

indicators.note: takes every other letter of fervent, starting from the first

explanation.surface: Someone is regularly fervent with worry.
explanation.definitionFit: To fret is to worry anxiously.

definitions.meaning: a thick drawing paper is sold under this name
a report is a loud bang, which a gun's shell produces when fired

explanation.surface: Someone asks which paper produces a written report.
explanation.definitionFit: Cartridge paper is heavy drawing paper, and a cartridge fired makes a loud report.

indicators.note: the last letter is cut off

parts.note: to gape is to stare open-mouthed

explanation.surface: Someone stares endlessly into space.
explanation.definitionFit: A gap is an empty space between things.

parts.note: a quid is British slang for one pound sterling

explanation.surface: A second pound is needed to pay for some seafood.
explanation.definitionFit: Squid is a cephalopod eaten as seafood, as in calamari.

definitions.meaning: a score is a group of that many
in cricket a boundary, a ball reaching the rope along the ground, is worth four runs, so five give this total

explanation.surface: A batter hits five boundaries in an innings.
explanation.definitionFit: A score is the number made by five fours, the runs from five cricket boundaries.

indicators.note: round signals the letters are turned around into a new order

parts.note: read as pals, its letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A friend's tour goes round and round.
explanation.definitionFit: A pulsator is something that throbs rhythmically, like a pump or heart.
